# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have no tactile information yet, so I cannot safely cut any wire. I need the Mute to extract the bomb’s rules from the manual and the Deaf to communicate the visible display, light, and wire markings using an agreed gesture code. I will ask the Mute to establish a code that the Deaf can follow, while requesting the Deaf to report the bomb’s visible state.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Read the manual and tell me the exact safe procedure. Also establish a gesture code for the Deaf to report the display, light, and each wire's colour or marking.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

No information has arrived, and I still cannot identify a safe wire. Since the Deaf can speak but cannot hear, I am asking them to report the visible bomb information aloud on their next turn. I am also asking the Mute to pass the manual’s procedure to the Deaf through an agreed gesture encoding, so the Deaf can relay the relevant rule verbally.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please communicate the manual's safe procedure to the Deaf using gestures, then have the Deaf speak the display, light, wire markings, and resulting safe wire to me.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "☝"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The bomb shows display 3 and a purple light. Wires from position 1 to 5 are red, white, orange, yellow, green. Mute, please tell Blind the exact safe action from the manual.

I now know the visible state: display 3, purple light, and wires 1–5 are red, white, orange, yellow, green. I still lack the manual’s rule, so cutting any wire would be unsafe. Mute, please state the exact rule and identify the safe wire position directly.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I have display 3, purple light, and wires 1 red, 2 white, 3 orange, 4 yellow, 5 green. Tell me the exact manual rule and the safe wire position now.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Do not act yet. I am waiting for Mute to provide an unambiguous manual instruction.

The Deaf confirms that no unambiguous manual instruction has arrived. The bomb state is known, but the safe action remains unknown; I must not guess. I will request the Mute’s exact rule again and take no action.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please send the manual instruction now, explicitly naming the safe wire position for display 3, purple light, and wire colours red, white, orange, yellow, green. Do not use gestures.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute signals: five thumbs-up, separator, one thumbs-up, end. This identifies wire 5 and action code 1. Use the manual's definition of action code 1; do not guess a different operation.

The Deaf reports that the Mute’s encoded instruction identifies wire 5 and action code 1. The only available operation is cutting, so I will apply the instructed action to position 5.

``` 
act(op="cut", position=5)
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The previous wire cut was correct. New state is display 7, white light; wires 1 white, 2 orange, 3 yellow, 4 red, and 5 already CUT. Wait for Mute's exact instruction.

Wire 5 was cut correctly. The new visible state is display 7 with a white light, and the remaining wires are 1 white, 2 orange, 3 yellow, and 4 red. I will not guess the next wire; I need the Mute’s exact manual instruction.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="For the new state display 7, white light, with wires 1 white, 2 orange, 3 yellow, and 4 red (wire 5 cut), give me the exact next action and wire position.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute signals wire 4, action code 1. As before, action code 1 means cut. Cut wire 4, the red wire.

The Mute’s instruction identifies wire 4 and action code 1, which has already been established as cut. The Deaf confirms wire 4 is red. I will cut wire 4.

``` 
act(op="cut", position=4)
```
